From 9198abdc2c5e0c4929545e4a69f714e6549b8ea6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Janos Villanyi <a74esev@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 29 May 2017 16:27:29 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] Fix premature closure of TCP connection

Fixes: #152 Premature closure of TCP connection

Clear the FIN flag for packets that are being dropped during so_rcv buffer
full condition.

This patch fixes a problem introduced by commit
af101aa4e648b020886fc36b51df4cc80e2c98a9 for bug #93 (Data corruption - tcp
packets dropped in the receive path).
If there is not enough room in the so_rcv sockbuf, the fix of bug #93
correctly drops the current packet to trigger a retransmit.
The problem occurs if that packet happens to be a FIN, in which case the
packet gets dropped but its FIN flag still gets processed, causing the
connection to close prematurely.
The patch below fixes the problem by clearing the FIN flag for such packets.

Signed-off-by: Janos Villanyi <a74esev@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Sorin Vultureanu <sorin.vultureanu@enea.com>

diff --git a/src/ofp_tcp_input.c b/src/ofp_tcp_input.c
index dc99541..04ba94d 100644
--- a/src/ofp_tcp_input.c
+++ b/src/ofp_tcp_input.c
@@ -2849,6 +2849,7 @@ dodata:							/* XXX */
 		} else {
 			odp_packet_free(m);
 			t_flags_or(tp->t_flags, TF_ACKNOW);
+			thflags &= ~OFP_TH_FIN;
 		}
 	} else {
 		odp_packet_free(m);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `src/ofp_tcp_input.c`**
   - A new line was added to clear the FIN flag from the TCP header flags (`thflags`) when a packet is dropped due to the `so_rcv` buffer being full. Specifically, the line `thflags &= ~OFP_TH_FIN;` was introduced right after the packet is freed.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification addresses a bug related to the premature closure of TCP connections. The change is a direct response to an issue caused by a previous fix (commit `af101aa4e648b020886fc36b51df4cc80e2c98a9`) that aimed to prevent data corruption by dropping packets when the receive buffer is full. The new line ensures that if a packet being dropped is a FIN packet, its FIN flag is cleared, preventing the connection from closing unexpectedly. This modification effectively resolves the unintended consequence of the earlier fix, maintaining the integrity of TCP connection management.
